purpose: Glimepiride is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is used along with a healthy diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a safe range. It is not used for type 1 diabetes or diabetic emergencies.
how_it_works: Your pancreas has special cells that make insulin, which is the hormone that lowers your blood sugar. Glimepiride tells your pancreas to release more insulin, especially after meals. This helps move sugar out of your blood and into your body's cells where it can be used for energy.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, dizzy, sweaty, confused, or hungry. Other side effects may include nausea, headache, and dizziness. Some people notice mild weight gain over time.
warnings: Low blood sugar is the biggest concern with this medicine — do not skip meals, and always carry a fast-acting sugar source like glucose tablets or juice. Tell your doctor if you drink alcohol, as it can increase your risk of low blood sugar. This medicine is not safe during pregnancy. Let your doctor know before any surgery or if you become sick, as your dose may need to change.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 1 mg to 2 mg taken once daily with breakfast or the first main meal of the day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to a maximum of 8 mg per day based on how your blood sugar responds. Always take it with food to reduce the risk of low blood sugar.
